notes: Countertop oven with five quartz elements and a convection fan; Breville's page marks the model discontinued. Breville and iFixit give 1,800 W for the oven as a whole, not per element, and the relay board parts come from one repair of a lightning-damaged unit.

gaps: The 1,800 W figure (Breville page, iFixit device page) is for the whole oven, so no w is set on the elements; the manual gives 1,800 W for toasting and 1,500 W for baking.
No voltage or AC rating is stated in the manual or on the device pages, so no v or ac is set.

Fan motor part SP0010500 rests on one iFixit community answer (May 2021), not on a Breville parts list, so it is left out. A comment in the same thread reads a motor label as SDR5812-01A15, 120 V 60 Hz 15 W. Both are unconfirmed leads.
No temperature sensor is claimed: the manual shows only the E03 and E04 error messages, not a sensor.
No relay is claimed: the repair guide names a relay board but shows no relay part. It gives no part numbers beyond the C114 E marking.
The materials of the wire rack and pizza pan are not stated; the manual describes the baking pan and broil rack as enamel.
PartSelect and ereplacementparts pages refused (HTTP 403). Part numbers seen only in search snippets (control board SP0024079, sensor SP0010508, power board SP0023060) are not claimed.
The manual describes an LCD and electronic dials, not a wind-up timer, so no timer switch is claimed.
method: Breville's own instruction book for the BOV800XL (EN and FR-CA, copyright Breville Pty. Ltd. 2023, code USC-M23), the breville.com copy linked from the Canada product page, read as text with research.js pdf. The copy on content.abt.com has identical text, so it is no longer cited.
Manual pages used (printed numbers): treated door glass on page 3, quartz tube elements on page 4, components and the wire rack on page 8, rack heights printed on the door window on page 11.
Also: convection fan assistance and the rack ejection note on page 16, enamel finish on page 27, enamel broil rack in the baking pan on page 28, outlet power on page 41.

Breville Canada product page for the BOV800 (breville.com/ca), read with WebFetch: five quartz elements, 1800 W preheat, inbuilt fan; the page itself is coded BOV800 and links the BOV800XL instruction book.
iFixit device page for the BOV800XL, read with WebFetch: 1800 W with 5 quartz elements, released 2011.
iFixit guide 157995 (BOV800XL relay board repair), read via /api/2.0/guides/157995 and the guide page.
iFixit answer 694078 (May 2021), read only for the SP0010500 lead.
Refused: PartSelect BOV800XL model page (HTTP 403) and ereplacementparts SP0023060 page (HTTP 403).

comps.spec: Five quartz elements (the manual calls them quartz tube elements)
Oven door glass, which the manual says is specially treated to be stronger than ordinary glass. The rack height positions are printed on the right side of the door window
Convection fan that circulates the hot air; the manual says convection cooking uses fan assistance
Wire rack, used with its spokes facing up; in the middle rack position the manual's Magnetic Auto-Eject Rack feature slides it halfway out when the door opens
12 x 12 in enamel broil rack (the manual mentions a porcelain enamel finish on the pan and rack); it sits inside the baking pan when broiling
12 x 12 in enamel baking pan with a porcelain enamel finish, supplied with the broil rack
13 in non-stick pizza pan (the manual mentions its non-stick coating)
Triac on the relay board; the repair guide says one of the small transistors on the board is technically a triac
Small transistors marked C114 E on the relay board, the number the repair guide says to order replacements by; transistor T203 was the one that failed in the guide's unit
